Let
\[
\delta=v^2+uw,\qquad a=v+w\delta,\qquad b=u-2v\delta-w\delta^2.
\]
Then
\[
a^2+wb=(v+w\delta)^2+w(u-2v\delta-w\delta^2)=v^2+uw=\delta,
\]
so
\[
u=b+2a(a^2+wb)-w(a^2+wb)^2,\qquad v=a-w(a^2+wb).
\]
Thus \(A=k[a,b,w]\).

Now rewrite the definitions:
\[
P=2b-a+2w,\qquad Q=3a-2w,\qquad 5w=5w.
\]
Also
\[
E=Q^2+5wP.
\]
For
\[
U=\sigma(u)=P+2QE-5wE^2,\quad V=\sigma(v)=Q-5wE,\quad W=\sigma(w)=5w,
\]
we have
\[
V^2+UW=E.
\]
Therefore the transformed \(a,b,w\)-coordinates are
\[
\sigma(a)=V+WE=Q=3a-2w,
\]
\[
\sigma(b)=U-2VE-WE^2=P=2b-a+2w,
\]
\[
\sigma(w)=5w.
\]
So \(\sigma\) is conjugate to the linear map
\[
(a,b,w)\mapsto (3a-2w,\;2b-a+2w,\;5w).
\]

Diagonalize this linear action using
\[
A_1=a+w,\qquad B_1=a+b,\qquad C_1=w.
\]
Then
\[
\sigma(A_1)=3A_1,\qquad \sigma(B_1)=2B_1,\qquad \sigma(C_1)=5C_1.
\]
Hence if \(F\in A^\sigma\), writing
\[
F=\sum c_{ijk}B_1^iA_1^jC_1^k
\]
gives
\[
c_{ijk}(2^i3^j5^k-1)=0
\]
for every \(i,j,k\). Since \(\operatorname{char} k=0\), this forces \(i=j=k=0\). Thus
\[
A^\sigma=k.
\]
Also \(\sigma\) has infinite order, since \(\sigma(B_1)=2B_1\).

Every element of \(R\) has a unique finite form
\[
z=\sum_{m,n\ge 0} a_{mn}x^m y^n,\qquad a_{mn}\in A.
\]
For \(f\in A\),
\[
x^m y^n f=\sigma^{m-n}(f)x^m y^n.
\]
If \(z\) commutes with all \(f\in A\), then any nonzero \(a_{mn}\) requires \(\sigma^{m-n}=\mathrm{id}\). Since \(\sigma\) has infinite order, this forces \(m=n\). Thus
\[
z=\sum_{n\ge 0} a_n(xy)^n.
\]
Commuting with \(x\) gives \(\sigma(a_n)=a_n\), so \(a_n\in A^\sigma=k\). Conversely, \(xy\) is central:
\[
xyf=x\sigma^{-1}(f)y=fxy,
\]
and \(xy\) commutes with \(x,y\) because \(yx=xy\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[xy]}.
\]
